readings: reset forces the state to A (so z=0 after reset)
reset forces the state to an unspecified state (e.g., E or F, giving z=1) because the reset state is never named
reset is synchronous and active-high: state updates to the reset state only on a positive clk edge while reset=1
reset is asynchronous and/or active-low: state changes immediately on reset assertion independent of clk, or the opposite reset polarity is used
z is a combinational Moore output of the current state, so it changes in the same cycle the state register updates
z is a registered output, so it can lag the state by one cycle depending on whether it is assigned from current or next state
z equals the parenthetical value shown for the current state: 1 for E and F, 0 for A, B, C, D
the parenthetical value is not explicitly stated to be z, so z could be assigned differently or left undefined
